thread:
maria: heads-up thread: i'm consolidating notes around "opaque leases" (compact signed tokens) and revocation strategies so infra/orgs can pick defaults for hosted/dedicated/private. goal: one short doc we can link from RFC.
kevin: +1. high-level choices i see: ttl-only (short-lived tokens), rev-list (explicit ids pushed), rev_seq (monotonic sequence via config-sync), hybrid (ttl + rev_seq). each has different perf/ops tradeoffs.
sara: constraints from private installs: no outbound validation calls, config-sync is the only reliable channel for pushes, and customers may opt for strict_denial if revocation state is stale. document must call that out.
aj: also consider emergency revocation (compromise) workflows. operators will want a low-latency handle. which strategies support that?
maria: summary: ttl-only -> simplest, immediate revocation only by short TTL (higher renew rps). rev-list -> supports targeted revocations but needs regular snapshot pushes; payload size + apply latency matters. rev_seq -> excellent for bulk invalidation (bump seq to invalidate broad classes) and works well with config-sync. hybrid -> best practical: short-ish ttl + rev_seq for urgent bulk revocations + occasional rev-list for rare targeted kills.
kevin: perf note: TTL of 5-15s is cheap for typical low-rps tenants but for high-throughput customers renew traffic can be significant. we need perf numbers per-tenancy tier. add perf-run items.
sara: security note: key rotation interplay with revocation must be explicit. rotation options: - rotate signing key and accept both keys for overlap window (shortening window opens risk) - rotate and increment rev_seq to force early invalidation. doc should recommend rotating via KMS + bump rev_seq where possible.
aj: operational playbook ask: how to push urgent revocations to private installs? idea: support a small revoke-list snapshot channel that is distributed via config-sync, with size limits and TTL on entries. private installs adopt best-effort.
maria: propose a recommendation block: - default (hosted): hybrid but leaning TTL=15s + rev_seq for control-plane bulk ops. allow permissive retry/refresh path when unreachable. - dedicated: similar to hosted but ops can choose TTL=5s if they favor security. - private: rev_seq-first with configurable strict_revocation flag. recommend longer TTLs to reduce renew churn if tenant selects permissive. document KMS rotation guidance.
kevin: telemetry: emit validation.latency, validation.result (accept/deny/allow-degraded), revoke_mismatch, rev_seq_age, key_id_used. console maps lease_id -> last_seen_runtime + decision.
sara: verifier semantics pseudo-code (short):
```
load(pubkeys)
if !verify(sig, pubkey) -> deny
if now < iat - skew || now > exp + skew -> deny
if token.rev > local.rev_seq:
  if strict_revocation: deny
  else: allow_with_audit
if token.id in local.revoke_list -> deny
allow
```
aj: replay protection: require nonce + small LRU cache of nonces in runtime. document memory/config knobs and default small window (e.g., 1k entries).
maria: rollout checklist (ops-bot please convert to backlog items): - spec token schema v1 (fields + size limits) - signer endpoint + key rotation docs - verifier libraries (go/rust/python) + unit tests - config-sync channels: pubkey snapshots, rev_seq, revoke_list snapshots - console mapping + telemetry dashboard - perf tests for TTL renew traffic and verifier latency - migration plan (runtime accepts probe + opaque-lease behind feature flag)
ops-bot: noted. creating backlog tasks: spec-opaque-lease-v1, signer-service, verifier-libs, config-sync-revseq, revoke-list-channel, console-lease-mapping, perf-renew-tests, rollout-rfc.
kevin: edge-cases: clock skew, clock rollback, long-queued requests (batches), and streaming sessions where a lease must be refreshable mid-stream. add a streaming-refresh section: streaming sessions carry a refresh-token handshake to request an extended lease without full rebind.
sara: privacy: do NOT include prompt content. include minimal audit fields: project_id, model_id, route_hint (optional), sample_hash (opt-in). add data-retention guidance for audit logs.
maria: i will assemble this into a single "revocation-handbook" doc with recommendation matrix, pseudo-code, ops checklist, and example tokens. plan to post draft to #rfc tomorrow. feedback welcome now so i can fold it in.
aj: :thumbsup: prefer hybrid default. please include perf numbers when you have them.
kevin: i'll attach perf estimates in the RFC after a quick benchmark.
sara: +1. also include short troubleshooting playbook for customers who report "routing mismatch". common causes: clock skew, stale rev_seq snapshot, key rollover pending.
maria: thanks all  i'll post the draft and link these notes.
